brief.text: You're the one with the rig. Good. Every light on this district runs down a wire, and I'm the man they call when the wire goes.
Here's the audition. Take the car, get down to the south substation, put the south block in the dark. Then get clean.

steps.label: Get in the car (F)
Drive to the south substation
Put the south block in the dark (H)
Lose the heat

debrief.text: Eight seconds of dark and nobody saw your face. That's the whole trade.
Somebody at Arden Holdings pays well for that kind of quiet. Celeste Marrow. She'll call.

brief.text: Ruf says you're discreet. I'm at the Hotel on Main. Come down to the door — I don't do business on the phone.

steps.label: Meet Celeste at the Hotel on Main

say.text: Arden Holdings owns most of the empty land on this district. Every lot you've watched go up, we bought when it was mud.
Walk with me to the plaza. There's one I want you to see.

steps.label: Walk the plaza lot with Celeste

say.text: Mud and a fence. By next year, forty storeys — if the neighbours stop filing objections.
Ground's broken. Every week that crane waits on a permit costs us more than you'll earn this year.
Watch it climb. That's what money looks like before it's finished.
Topped out and let before the glass went in. That's how it's supposed to go. It rarely does.
The objections all come from one block on West Avenue. I need names — who still lives there, who's organising. Go and look.

steps.label: Put names to 3 people on West Avenue
Nell has noticed you — answer her

say.text: You've been reading my neighbours off that little screen for ten minutes. I run the bookshop. I notice people who read.
You're Arden's, aren't you. So: do those names go to Celeste Marrow, or do you tell me what she's planning?

options.text: It's a job. The names go to Arden.
options.note: You gave Arden the names on West Avenue.

reply.text: Then get off my street. Arden will have this shop by spring, and you can tell people you helped.

options.text: She wants the whole block. Here's what I know.
options.note: You told Nell what Arden is planning.

reply.text: The whole block. Of course she does. Right — you're going to help me make that very expensive.

debrief.text: Twelve names by morning. Arden appreciates people who finish things.
No names? Then you're paid for the walk and nothing else. Think harder next time.

brief.text: Arden's permit on the south lots lapses if the site sits idle for a working week. The inspector drives past every afternoon.
So the crane doesn't turn while he's looking. Go south, find Arden's crane, and kill the power while it's working.

steps.label: Stop Arden's crane: black out the south block while it works
Lose the heat

debrief.text: The inspector wrote 'no activity on site'. One more day on Arden's clock.
Come by the shop some time. First book's free. The second one, I'll judge you by.

brief.text: The West Avenue tenants meet at the bookshop tonight. Their lawyer keeps the paperwork on a machine in the back.
My people need four minutes inside with the lights off. Be at the bookshop, and kill the north block when you get there.

steps.label: Go to West Ave Books
Kill the north block (H)
Lose the heat

debrief.text: The files are gone. Without paper, the tenants are just people who are upset. That passes.

brief.text: The plaza lot goes to auction Friday. Arden's bidding. The tenants have a land trust and a counter-bid. Both get filed at the registry.
Kill the north block, then the south while the north still burns, and the registry's backup goes too. No filings for a week. Nell gets her week.
Kill the north block, then the south while the north still burns, and the registry's backup goes too. The trust misses its deadline. Arden won't.

steps.label: Get in the car (F)
Drive to the plaza
Black out the north block, then the south while it burns
Lose the heat

debrief.text: Registry's dark, backup's dark. Whatever happens Friday happens because of us. Go home. I'll call.

brief.text: Ruf wasn't buying me a week. While the registry was dark he walked in with a key card and filed Arden's bid by hand.
He drinks at the tavern on Main. Go and ask him what he's worth.
Ruf filed our bid, as agreed. He also kept a ledger of every payment Arden ever made him, and he's selling it tonight.
He drinks at the tavern on Main. Go and remind him who he works for.

steps.label: Find Ruf at the Tavern on Main

say.text: Sit down. You look like you've been talking to people.

steps.label: Decide what happens to Ruf's ledger

say.text: Arden pays for everything on this district. The cranes, the inspectors, the patrols. Me. It's all in here.
Arden would pay a fortune to watch it burn. The tenants would use it to void every permit Arden holds. Your call. I'm tired.

options.text: Sell the ledger back to Arden.
options.note: You sold Ruf's ledger back to Arden. The plaza lot is theirs.

reply.text: Smart. Celeste will send a car. Nobody on West Avenue will ever know it existed.

options.note: You gave Ruf's ledger to Nell. Arden's bid on the plaza lot is void.

reply.text: Then I'd get off this district before Arden reads the papers. I know I will.

brief.text: The ledger's with the city attorney. Arden's bid is void and the plaza lot goes to the land trust. Come and see it.
You sold my neighbours' names, then brought me the thing that saves them. I don't know what you are. Come to the plaza lot.

steps.label: Meet Nell at the plaza lot

say.text: Mud, still. Forty homes one day, and nobody's rent tied to somebody else's spreadsheet.
Arden's crane, our building. We're keeping the crane driver. He was the only one who ever waved.
Arden finished it for us and hasn't worked that out yet. Forty homes.
The shop stays open. Come by. First book's still free.
We're square now. Don't come to West Avenue again.

brief.text: The ledger's ash and the plaza lot is ours. Come and see what you bought. You paid for it too.

steps.label: Meet Celeste at the plaza lot

say.text: Mud today. Next year, forty storeys and a doorman. Nobody will remember what the block looked like.
Every floor that crane lifts is a floor West Avenue can't afford. That isn't cruelty. It's arithmetic.
Topped out, and let before the glass went in.
You started on the wrong side and finished on the right one. Arden remembers both.
Arden owns more lots than this one. I'll call.
